genZNote: Colonies literally black — the one Aspergillus you can call by color alone and be right.

morphology.shape: Filamentous mold with radiating conidial heads
morphology.size: Hyphae ~3-6 µm wide; conidiophores up to several hundred µm
morphology.notes: Large, dark brown to black biseriate conidial heads ("aspergillus head") with radiating chains of dark spores

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, decaying vegetation, and stored grain worldwide
habitat.hostAssociation: Environmental saprophyte; opportunistic pathogen and common food/industrial contaminant
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: One of the most common environmental molds; used industrially to produce citric acid

microscopy.appearance: Septate hyphae with large biseriate conidial heads bearing chains of black-brown conidia

culture.colonyMorphology: Initially white/yellow, becoming carbon-black to dark brown and granular as conidia mature
culture.pigmentation: Black to dark brown surface, pale reverse

identificationClues: Rapidly growing black mold on Sabouraud agar
Biseriate conidial heads with radiating chains of black conidia on microscopy
Common cause of otomycosis (fungal ear infection)
Often a laboratory/environmental contaminant, complicating interpretation of positive cultures

diseases: Aspergilloma (fungus ball, often in a pre-existing lung cavity)
Invasive aspergillosis (rare, in severely immunocompromised hosts)
Allergic bronchopulmonary reaction in sensitized individuals
clinicalImportance.transmission: Inhalation of airborne conidia; direct contact for otomycosis
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common environmental molds; generally less pathogenic than A. fumigatus but an important cause of otomycosis and occasional invasive disease in the severely immunosuppressed
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Because it is a ubiquitous environmental contaminant, isolation from a non-sterile site must be interpreted alongside clinical findings

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — identified by colony/microscopic morphology
examFacts.importantTest: Lactophenol cotton blue mount showing biseriate black conidial heads
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Distinctive carbon-black colony color distinguishes it from A. fumigatus (blue-green) and A. flavus (yellow-green)
